syndromes.syndrome: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis: psychiatric symptoms, memory/speech deficits, seizures, dyskinesias, decreased consciousness, autonomic instability, central hypoventilation

demographics: 95% younger than 45 y and 37% younger than 18 y; female:male ~4:1, less marked in children <12 and adults >45 (Graus 2016, citing Titulaer 2013)

tumors.frequencyText: Overall 38% (PNS-Care); 58% in women >18 y; 0–5% in children <12 y (Graus 2016)
Tumors in 23% of adults >45 y, usually carcinomas rather than teratomas (Graus 2016)

cancerScreening: Women: screen for ovarian teratoma (pelvic imaging per local protocol)
Adults >45 y: screen for carcinoma
Consider rescreening in relapsing or refractory disease (PNS-Care 2021)

rationale: CSF positive in 250/250 vs serum 214/250 (sensitivity 100% vs 85.6%) on paired samples (Gresa-Arribas 2014)
Test both serum and CSF; CSF screening is obligatory for suspected surface-antibody encephalitis (PNS-Care 2021)
methodNotes: Surface antibody positive in serum only (CSF negative): confirm with tissue IHC or a research laboratory before calling it definite (PNS-Care 2021)
IgG against GluN1 is the relevant antibody (Graus 2016)

typicalFindings: Lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein, or oligoclonal bands
Often normal or nonspecific; may show transient cortical/subcortical FLAIR changes

otherTests: EEG: abnormal in 90% (432/482) (Titulaer 2013); extreme delta brush supports the diagnosis (Graus 2016 criteria)
pearls: Good outcome (mRS 0–2) in 81% (203/252) at 24 months; recovery can continue for up to 18 months
Second-line immunotherapy (rituximab, cyclophosphamide) is usually effective when first-line fails; early treatment and no ICU admission predict good outcome
Relapse risk 12% within 2 years; 67% of relapses milder than the first episode (Titulaer 2013)
Titers fall with recovery but often stay positive (24/28 CSF, 17/23 serum after recovery) — persistent positivity alone doesn't define activity
CSF titer change tracks relapse better than serum (14/19 vs 7/16); higher titers with teratoma or poor outcome (Gresa-Arribas 2014)
sources: Titulaer MJ, et al. Treatment and prognostic factors for long-term outcome in patients with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis: an observational cohort study. Lancet Neurol 2013;12(2):157-165. doi:10.1016/S1474-4422(12)70310-1

syndromes.syndrome: Faciobrachial dystonic seizures (47%) and subtle focal seizures (66%), usually before memory loss
Cognitive impairment without encephalitis criteria (up to 13%)

demographics: 66% male (25/38); median onset 64 y (range 31–84) (van Sonderen 2016)

tumors.frequencyText: 11% (4/36) in van Sonderen 2016, relation to LGI1 uncertain; <10%, mainly Morvan with LGI1 + CASPR2 (PNS-Care)

cancerScreening: Comprehensive cancer screening at initial diagnosis is sufficient for lower-risk antibodies (PNS-Care 2021)

rationale: Serum positive in 38/38 by CBA and IHC; CSF positive in only 9/17 (53%) by CBA and 15/17 by IHC (van Sonderen 2016)
CSF-only positivity in 8% of paired samples (Ariño 2016) — send both, but never rely on CSF alone
methodNotes: Antibodies are IgG4 (Ariño 2016)

normalPercentText: Pleocytosis >5 cells/μL in 16% (5/32) and protein >0.58 g/L in 16% (5/32) (van Sonderen 2016)
typicalFindings: When abnormal: mild pleocytosis (max 88 cells/μL) or mildly raised protein
Intrathecal IgG synthesis rare (Graus 2016)
Unilateral (60%) or bilateral (14%) hippocampal T2 lesions; mesial temporal sclerosis at follow-up in 7/16 (44%) with initial hippocampal lesions (text; Table 1 lists denominator 17)
Initial MRI can be normal with later limbic changes (Ariño 2016)

otherTests: EEG: epileptic activity 31%, focal slowing 25% (11/36, 9/36); FBDS have no EEG correlate
pearls: FBDS often precede memory loss — treating early is the window

Substantial response in 80%, but relapses in 35% (up to 8 y later); 86% have persistent amnesia for the illness, most survivors have mild residual cognitive deficit; 2-y case fatality 19% (van Sonderen 2016)
VGKC-complex antibodies without LGI1/CASPR2 are not syndrome-specific and don't prove autoimmunity (Graus 2016)
Serum LGI1 antibodies can persist after full recovery (Ariño 2016)
sources: van Sonderen A, et al. Anti-LGI1 encephalitis: clinical syndrome and long-term follow-up. Neurology 2016;87(14):1449-1456. doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000003173

syndromes.syndrome: Cerebellar dysfunction, neuropathic pain, insomnia, dysautonomia, weight loss

demographics: 89% male (34/38); median onset 66 y; women younger (median 49 vs 68 y) (van Sonderen 2016)

tumors.frequencyText: 19% overall (van Sonderen 2016); ~50% malignant thymoma in Morvan syndrome, LE almost always nonparaneoplastic (PNS-Care)

cancerScreening: Comprehensive cancer screening at initial diagnosis is sufficient for lower-risk antibodies (PNS-Care 2021)
Morvan syndrome: treated as intermediate risk by PNS-Care — screen for thymoma

rationale: Serum positive with both CBA and IHC in all 38 patients (van Sonderen 2016)
CSF IHC was negative in 3 patients, all with tumor and Morvan syndrome
methodNotes: IgG4 in all; IgG1 also in 63% (van Sonderen 2016)

typicalFindings: Mild pleocytosis (6–20 cells/μL) in 7 patients

normalPercentText: Unremarkable in 70% of patients with cognitive decline or seizures (van Sonderen 2016)
typicalFindings: Bilateral medial temporal T2 hyperintensity in 24%

otherTests: EMG/nerve conduction for peripheral nerve hyperexcitability
pearls: Seven core features: encephalopathy (cognitive/seizures), cerebellar dysfunction, peripheral nerve hyperexcitability, dysautonomia, insomnia, neuropathic pain, weight loss — ≥3 in 77%
Slow course: median time to nadir 4 months, >1 year in 30%
Treatment response 93%; relapses 25% (van Sonderen 2016)
sources: van Sonderen A, et al. The clinical spectrum of Caspr2 antibody-associated disease. Neurology 2016;87(5):521-528. doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000002917

syndromes.syndrome: Limbic encephalitis with prominent seizures (95% eventually)

demographics: Male:female 12:8; patients without SCLC younger (median 39 y) than those with SCLC (median 67.5 y) (Höftberger 2013)
Paraneoplastic cases mostly older men who smoke; most young patients are not paraneoplastic (PNS-Care)
cancerScreening: Screen at diagnosis; if negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years when a high-risk phenotype (e.g., limbic encephalitis) occurs with older age, smoking, or a concurrent high-risk antibody (PNS-Care 2021)
Chest CT (± PET) for SCLC

rationale: Paired samples: CSF positive 12/12 vs serum 8/12 (Höftberger 2013)
Pooled: CSF 98.3% (71/72) vs serum 88.1% (69/77) (McKay 2019)
methodNotes: Surface antibody positive in serum only (CSF negative): confirm with tissue IHC or a research laboratory before calling it definite (PNS-Care 2021)
Co-occurring KCTD16 antibodies point to a paraneoplastic case (PNS-Care)

typicalFindings: Pleocytosis + raised protein 7/19, pleocytosis only 6/19, protein only 1/19 (Höftberger 2013)
Pooled: pleocytosis 59.3%, raised protein 43.9% (McKay 2019)
Hippocampal/amygdala FLAIR/T2 signal (LE pattern) 9/19; pial/cortical enhancement 2/19; leukoencephalopathy 1/19
Pooled: temporal T2 hyperintensity 54.8% (McKay 2019)

pearls: SCLC patients often carry additional onconeuronal antibodies (Ri, amphiphysin, SOX1) (Höftberger 2013)
Long-term prognosis is driven by the tumor; most improve with immunotherapy ± oncologic treatment (15/19)
sources: Höftberger R, et al. Encephalitis and GABAB receptor antibodies: novel findings in a new case series of 20 patients. Neurology 2013;81(17):1500-1506. doi:10.1212/WNL.0b013e3182a9585f

demographics: Median 62 y (23–81); 14/22 female (Höftberger 2015)

tumors.tumor: Lung cancer (incl. SCLC), thymoma, breast, ovarian teratoma
tumors.frequencyText: 64% (14/22): 5 lung, 4 thymoma, 2 breast, 2 ovarian teratoma pathologic + 1 lung radiologic (Höftberger 2015); >50% SCLC and malignant thymoma (PNS-Care)

cancerScreening: Screen at diagnosis; if negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years when a high-risk phenotype (e.g., limbic encephalitis) occurs with older age, smoking, or a concurrent high-risk antibody (PNS-Care 2021)

rationale: Paired samples: CSF 14/14 vs serum 10/14 positive (Höftberger 2015)
methodNotes: Surface antibody positive in serum only (CSF negative): confirm with tissue IHC or a research laboratory before calling it definite (PNS-Care 2021)

normalPercentText: Normal cell count and protein in 27% (6/22) (Höftberger 2015, Table 1)
typicalFindings: Pleocytosis 11/22 (median 23 cells/μL); isolated protein elevation 5/22
LE: unilateral or bilateral mesiotemporal FLAIR/T2 hyperintensity (11/12)
Diffuse encephalitis: multifocal cortical, basal ganglia, thalamic, hypothalamic, or callosal lesions

pearls: Coexisting onconeuronal antibodies predicted poor outcome; all 5 deaths had tumor or additional paraneoplastic symptoms
Response: 5 good, 10 partial, 6 none (n=21)
Relapses occurred only without aggressive therapy (0/19 vs 6/18) (Höftberger 2015)
sources: Höftberger R, et al. Encephalitis and AMPA receptor antibodies: novel findings in a case series of 22 patients. Neurology 2015;84(24):2403-2412. doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000001682

syndromes.syndrome: Encephalitis with seizures (88%) and refractory status epilepticus
Cognitive, behavioral, consciousness changes; movement disorders (more in children)

demographics: Children and adults: median 40.5 y; children median 13 y, adults median 59 y; 50% female (Spatola 2017)
cancerScreening: Comprehensive cancer screening at initial diagnosis is sufficient for lower-risk antibodies (PNS-Care 2021)
Adults: screen for thymoma

rationale: Paired samples: both positive 14/16, serum-only 2/16, none CSF-only (Spatola 2017)

typicalFindings: Pleocytosis, elevated protein, or oligoclonal bands
Multifocal, asynchronous cortical-subcortical T2/FLAIR lesions in 77% — temporal (95%) and frontal (65%), also basal ganglia

pearls: Multifocal cortical-subcortical MRI lesions are the diagnostic clue
Children: more often post-viral (post-HSV, HHV6, with coexisting NMDAR antibodies); adults: tumor-related
Substantial improvement in 18/21; 3 died (Spatola 2017)
sources: Spatola M, et al. Investigations in GABAA receptor antibody-associated encephalitis. Neurology 2017;88(11):1012-1020. doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000003713

syndromes.syndrome: Prodromal weight loss/diarrhea → cognitive-mental dysfunction + CNS hyperexcitability (hyperekplexia, myoclonus, tremor, seizures); triad in 67%

demographics: Median 57 y, 8/9 male (Hara 2017); median 53 y, 12/20 men (Tobin 2014)
cancerScreening: Comprehensive cancer screening at initial diagnosis is sufficient for lower-risk antibodies (PNS-Care 2021)

rationale: Serum positive in 20/20; CSF positive in all 7 tested (Tobin 2014)
methodNotes: IgG4 and IgG1 in all (Hara 2017)

normalPercentText: No pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands in 4/9 (Hara 2017, table)
typicalFindings: Pleocytosis 5/9 (6–130 cells/μL; median 12); intrathecal IgG synthesis 2/5
Nonspecific white-matter T2/FLAIR changes in 3/9; temporal atrophy 1/9

otherTests: GI evaluation for unexplained diarrhea/weight loss
pearls: Unexplained weight loss (median 20 kg) or diarrhea preceding neurologic symptoms (median 4 months) is the clue
Peak may come late (median 8 months); relapses in 23%, immunotherapy-responsive (Hara 2017)
sources: Hara M, et al. DPPX antibody-associated encephalitis: main syndrome and antibody effects. Neurology 2017;88(14):1340-1348. doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000003796

syndromes.syndrome: Progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus (PERM) — majority
Stiff-person syndrome, limbic encephalitis/epileptic encephalopathy, brainstem syndromes

demographics: 24 male / 21 female; age 1–75 y (median 50) (Carvajal-González 2014)

tumors.frequencyText: <10% (PNS-Care); new tumors in 4/45: 3 thymoma, 1 B-cell marginal zone lymphoma (Carvajal-González 2014)

cancerScreening: Comprehensive cancer screening at initial diagnosis is sufficient for lower-risk antibodies (PNS-Care 2021)

rationale: Serum levels higher than (10/11) or equal to (1/11) CSF; intrathecal synthesis in all 6 pairs studied (Carvajal-González 2014)
methodNotes: Brain IHC isn't useful for GlyR — rely on CBA (PNS-Care 2021)
Very low serum titers with alternative diagnoses were excluded from the cohort — interpret low titers with caution

typicalFindings: Pleocytosis 13/30, raised protein 4/30, oligoclonal bands 6/30

normalPercentText: Brain MRI normal in 72% (26/36); spinal MRI normal in 18/23 (Carvajal-González 2014)
typicalFindings: Generally uninformative: white-matter lesions, atrophy, small-vessel disease
Spinal cord: short/patchy lesions 4/23, one longitudinally extensive

pearls: Most improve markedly with immunotherapy (median mRS 5 → 1), but 4/45 died acutely and relapses occur — maintenance immunosuppression may be needed
Can coexist with high-titer GAD65 antibodies (4 patients)
sources: Carvajal-González A, et al. Glycine receptor antibodies in PERM and related syndromes: characteristics, clinical features and outcomes. Brain 2014;137(8):2178-2192. doi:10.1093/brain/awu142
Graus F, et al. Updated diagnostic criteria for paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes (PNS-Care). Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2021;8:e1014. doi:10.1212/NXI.0000000000001014

syndromes.syndrome: Encephalitis with psychiatric (10/11) and cognitive (10/11) symptoms, movement disorders (7/11), sleep dysfunction (7/11), seizures (6/11) — not restricted to LE
Limbic encephalitis with Hodgkin lymphoma (Ophelia syndrome)

demographics: Median 29 y (6–75); 5/11 female (Spatola 2018)
cancerScreening: Screen at diagnosis; if negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years when a high-risk phenotype occurs with older age, smoking, or a concurrent high-risk antibody (PNS-Care 2021)
Screen for Hodgkin lymphoma (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis ± PET per local protocol)

rationale: No paired serum/CSF sensitivity data in the sources read; PNS-Care recommends testing both for surface antibodies
methodNotes: Surface antibody positive in serum only (CSF negative): confirm with tissue IHC or a research laboratory before calling it definite (PNS-Care 2021)

typicalFindings: Limbic (1/5) or extralimbic (4/5) involvement

pearls: Median peak mRS 4; 4/11 needed ICU care, yet at median 48 months 6 recovered completely and 5 partially
Relapses in 2/11 (Spatola 2018)
sources: Spatola M, et al. Encephalitis with mGluR5 antibodies: symptoms and antibody effects. Neurology 2018;90(22):e1964-e1972. doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000005614
Graus F, et al. Updated diagnostic criteria for paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes (PNS-Care). Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2021;8:e1014. doi:10.1212/NXI.0000000000001014

syndromes.syndrome: Cerebellar syndrome with behavioral/cognitive or other neurologic symptoms (86%)

demographics: Median onset 55 y (IQR 43–64); 43% female (n=30) (Spatola 2020)
cancerScreening: Comprehensive cancer screening at initial diagnosis is sufficient for lower-risk antibodies (PNS-Care 2021)

rationale: No paired serum/CSF sensitivity data in the sources read; PNS-Care recommends testing both
methodNotes: Surface antibody positive in serum only (CSF negative): confirm with tissue IHC or a research laboratory before calling it definite (PNS-Care 2021)
Antibodies mainly IgG1 (Spatola 2020)

typicalFindings: Pleocytosis 11/25 (median 27 cells/mm³); oligoclonal bands or raised IgG index 11/20
Cerebellar atrophy at follow-up in 10/12 (83%)

pearls: Outcome (n=25): stabilization 52%, significant improvement 40%, 2 died — long-term disability and cerebellar atrophy are common
Worse initial disability (needing walking assistance, higher SARA) predicted bad outcome — treat early (Spatola 2020)
sources: Spatola M, et al. Clinical features, prognostic factors, and antibody effects in anti-mGluR1 encephalitis. Neurology 2020;95(22):e3012-e3025. doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000010854
Graus F, et al. Updated diagnostic criteria for paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes (PNS-Care). Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2021;8:e1014. doi:10.1212/NXI.0000000000001014

syndromes.syndrome: Sleep disorder: NREM/REM parasomnia with sleep-breathing difficulty (36% at diagnosis; all eventually had sleep problems)
Bulbar syndrome: dysphagia, sialorrhea, stridor, acute respiratory insufficiency (27%)

demographics: Median 64 y (46–83) (Gaig 2017)
cancerScreening: No cancer association established (1 hypernephroma in 22)

rationale: Paired samples: both positive 14/16, serum-only 2/16 (both PSP-like) (Gaig 2017)
methodNotes: IgG4 predominates (16/21); IgG1 + IgG4 in 20/21

typicalFindings: Pleocytosis 6/20 (30%); raised protein 10/20 (50%, median 64 mg/dL); intrathecal oligoclonal bands 1/14 (Gaig 2017)
Mild brainstem/cerebellar atrophy 3/22; bilateral hippocampal atrophy with FLAIR signal 1/22

otherTests: Video-polysomnography: undifferentiated NREM parasomnia, RBD in 8/9, obstructive sleep apnea in 16/16 (median AHI 33), stridor in 10/12 (Gaig 2017)
HLA typing: DRB1*10:01 and DQB1*05:01 in 13/15 (87%)
pearls: Mimics a neurodegenerative disorder (PSP, chronic sleep disorder) — the antibody is missed unless considered
Only 2/20 treated patients had mild, transient improvement; 13/22 (59%) died — 6 suddenly, 6 from aspiration pneumonia (Gaig 2017)
Stridor and sleep apnea are near-universal — PSG with audio; consider airway/CPAP planning
sources: Gaig C, et al. Clinical manifestations of the anti-IgLON5 disease. Neurology 2017;88(18):1736-1743. doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000003887

syndromes.syndrome: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome: proximal leg-predominant weakness, autonomic dysfunction (~90%), reduced reflexes that improve after exercise

tumors.frequencyText: ~50% in LEMS; nearly 90% with rapidly progressive cerebellar syndrome (PNS-Care)

cancerScreening: Screen at diagnosis; if negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years when a high-risk phenotype occurs with older age, smoking, or a concurrent high-risk antibody (PNS-Care 2021)

LEMS (Titulaer 2011): CT thorax + FDG-PET at diagnosis, then repeat; DELTA-P 0–1 → stop after two adequate negative screens (second at 6 months); 2 → every 6 months for 2 years; 3–6 → second screen at 3 months, then every 6 months for 2 years

rationale: Present in nearly 90% of LEMS, similarly in paraneoplastic and nonparaneoplastic forms (PNS-Care)
methodNotes: Brain IHC isn't useful for P/Q VGCC antibodies (PNS-Care)
SOX1 antibodies in LEMS strongly suggest SCLC; N-type VGCC co-occurrence may be slightly more common in paraneoplastic LEMS (PNS-Care)

otherTests: Electrodiagnostic confirmation of LEMS is required (PNS-Care)
pearls: DELTA-P (1 point each, at or within 3 months of onset): age ≥50, smoking at diagnosis, weight loss ≥5%, bulbar involvement, erectile dysfunction, Karnofsky <70 — 0–1 points = 0–2.6% SCLC; 4, 5, 6 points = 93.5%, 96.6%, 100% (Titulaer 2011)
LEMS + VGCC without cancer is 'probable' PNS; upgrade if SCLC appears within 2 years, downgrade to 'possible' after >2 years without cancer (PNS-Care)
sources: Graus F, et al. Updated diagnostic criteria for paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes (PNS-Care). Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2021;8:e1014. doi:10.1212/NXI.0000000000001014

Titulaer MJ, et al. Clinical Dutch-English Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS) tumor association prediction score accurately predicts small-cell lung cancer in the LEMS. J Clin Oncol 2011;29(7):902-908. doi:10.1200/JCO.2010.32.0440

demographics: Paraneoplastic cases are older, more often male, with associated neuronal antibodies and atypical presentations (PNS-Care)

tumors.tumor: SCLC, other neuroendocrine tumors, malignant thymoma
tumors.frequencyText: <15% (PNS-Care); cancer association mainly with LE, men >50 (Graus 2016)

cancerScreening: Comprehensive cancer screening at initial diagnosis is sufficient for lower-risk antibodies (PNS-Care 2021)
GAD65-associated SPS: call it paraneoplastic only if the tumor expresses GAD65 (PNS-Care)

rationale: High-concentration group defined as serum >10,000 IU/mL (ELISA) or CSF >100 IU/mL; classic syndromes in 34/36 (94%) (Muñoz-Lopetegi 2020)
Above these cutoffs, ELISA agreed with IHC and CBA (CSF 100 IU/mL: 100% concordance; serum 10,000 IU/mL: 97–100%)
Low titers, especially with atypical phenotypes, make alternative diagnoses more likely
methodNotes: Low-titer GAD65 is common in type 1 diabetes — interpret with titer and phenotype
Confirm commercial line-blot/CBA positives with brain IHC, especially with low titer, serum-only testing, or a mismatched phenotype (PNS-Care 2021)

typicalFindings: High-titer group: oligoclonal bands 12/18 (67%), pleocytosis 6/27 (22%), raised protein 8/24 (33%) (Muñoz-Lopetegi 2020)

pearls: High-titer patients mostly improve with immunotherapy but rarely recover completely
Falling serum concentration tracked clinical improvement (15/17 fell, 14 improved; the 2 unchanged didn't improve) (Muñoz-Lopetegi 2020)
sources: Muñoz-Lopetegi A, et al. Neurologic syndromes related to anti-GAD65: clinical and serologic response to treatment. Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2020;7(3):e696. doi:10.1212/NXI.0000000000000696

syndromes.syndrome: Stiff-person phenomena (39% of women, 12% of men; full SPS criteria in 10% and 4%)

demographics: Isolated amphiphysin-IgG (19/63): more often women with breast cancer, myelopathy, or stiff-person phenomena (Pittock 2005)

tumors.frequencyText: ~80% (PNS-Care); cancer in 50/63: SCLC 27, breast 16, NSCLC 1, melanoma 2 (Pittock 2005)

cancerScreening: High-risk antibody: if initial screening is negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years (PNS-Care 2021)
Chest CT and breast imaging

rationale: Cohort identified by serum testing (Pittock 2005); PNS-Care recommends testing both serum and CSF
methodNotes: Intracellular antigen: confirm with immunoblot after tissue IHC (PNS-Care)
Coexisting paraneoplastic antibodies in 74% — they predict the tumor (Pittock 2005)

typicalFindings: Pleocytosis 13/28 (mean 22 cells/μL); raised protein 10/28 (mean 104 mg/dL); oligoclonal bands 5/28
Spinal cord: intrinsic lesions in 5/25 with symptomatic myelopathy, 4 longitudinally extensive (3 enhancing); normal spinal MRI doesn't exclude myelopathy (2/20)

pearls: Paraneoplastic SPS with amphiphysin: older patients, more neck and upper-limb involvement than GAD65 SPS (PNS-Care)
Amphiphysin or CV2/CRMP5 can replace Hu in some LE with SCLC (Graus 2016)
Improvement documented with tumor therapy in some and with IV steroids/IVIG in a few; 13/63 died during follow-up (Pittock 2005)
sources: Pittock SJ, et al. Amphiphysin autoimmunity: paraneoplastic accompaniments. Ann Neurol 2005;58(1):96-107. doi:10.1002/ana.20529

demographics: Median 63 y (28–82); 75% men (Graus 2001, n=200)
LE with Hu antibodies is usually nonparaneoplastic in patients <18 y (PNS-Care)

tumors.tumor: SCLC >> NSCLC, other neuroendocrine tumors, neuroblastoma

cancerScreening: High-risk antibody: if initial screening is negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years (PNS-Care 2021)
Chest CT ± FDG-PET for SCLC

rationale: Onconeuronal antibodies are usually detected in serum; PNS-Care recommends testing serum and CSF
methodNotes: Intracellular antigen: tissue IHC/IF with confirmatory immunoblot; confirm commercial line-blot positives with IHC, especially at low titer or with a mismatched phenotype (PNS-Care 2021)

normalPercentText: Pooled Hu/Yo/CV2/Ri/Ma/Tr cohort: CSF abnormal in 93% (n=295); profile similar across antibody types (Psimaras 2010)
typicalFindings: Pleocytosis more often early: 47% before vs 28% after month 3; oligoclonal bands the only abnormality in 10%
Brainstem encephalitis subgroup: MRI normal in 22/22; pleocytosis in only 2/19 (Saiz 2009)
Overall MRI frequencies not reported in Graus 2001

pearls: Improvement or stabilization: 37.5% with tumor treatment ± immunotherapy, 20.6% with immunotherapy alone, 11.6% untreated; tumor treatment was the independent predictor (OR 4.56) (Graus 2001)
Treat the cancer early while the patient is still independent
sources: Graus F, et al. Updated diagnostic criteria for paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes (PNS-Care). Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2021;8:e1014. doi:10.1212/NXI.0000000000001014

syndromes.syndrome: Painful asymmetric axonal polyradiculoneuropathy (65% of CRMP5 neuropathy), often months before the cancer
Peripheral neuropathy (47%), autonomic neuropathy (31%), cerebellar ataxia (26%), subacute dementia (25%)
Chorea (11%); cranial neuropathy (17%) incl. loss of smell/taste and optic neuropathy

demographics: Patients with thymoma are younger and more often have myasthenia gravis, less often neuropathy (PNS-Care)
cancerScreening: High-risk antibody: if initial screening is negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years (PNS-Care 2021)
Chest CT ± FDG-PET (SCLC, thymoma)

rationale: CSF positive in 27/27 tested; CSF titer equaled or exceeded paired serum in 10 (Yu 2001)
methodNotes: Intracellular antigen: tissue IHC/IF with confirmatory immunoblot; confirm commercial line-blot positives with IHC, especially at low titer or with a mismatched phenotype (PNS-Care 2021)

typicalFindings: Lymphocytic pleocytosis (8–370/mm³), raised protein (47–400 mg/dL), raised IgG index or synthesis rate
CRMP5 neuropathy: inflammatory CSF in 92% vs 60% with Hu alone (Dubey 2018)
Brain MRI frequencies not reported in Yu 2001

pearls: Multifocal neuraxis involvement; chorea or vision loss in a smoker should prompt testing
Can replace Hu in some LE with SCLC (Graus 2016)

Neuropathy: impairment score worsened in 71%; improved in 21% (NIS) and 7% (mRS). Only high-dose IV steroids were linked to improvement/stabilization (63% vs 15%); immunotherapy relieved neuropathic pain (80% vs 20%) — Class IV (Dubey 2018)
Better 5-year survival than ANNA-1/Hu (67% vs 32%) (Dubey 2018)

syndromes.syndrome: Brainstem/cerebellar syndrome — gait instability is the commonest first symptom (86%)
Jaw-opening dystonia and/or laryngospasm (25% in Pittock 2003; 19% in Pittock 2010)

demographics: 10 men / 18 women (Pittock 2003); breast cancer in women, lung cancer in men (PNS-Care)
cancerScreening: High-risk antibody: if initial screening is negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years (PNS-Care 2021)
Breast imaging in women; chest CT ± FDG-PET

rationale: Cohort defined by serum immunofluorescence screening (Pittock 2003); PNS-Care recommends serum and CSF
methodNotes: Intracellular antigen: tissue IHC/IF with confirmatory immunoblot; confirm commercial line-blot positives with IHC, especially at low titer or with a mismatched phenotype (PNS-Care 2021)
Coexisting paraneoplastic antibodies in 73% (Hu, ANNA-3, CRMP5, P/Q and N-type VGCC, AChR) (Pittock 2003)

typicalFindings: Ri cohort (n=19): raised protein 37%, mild lymphocytosis 42% (Pittock 2003)
Pooled Hu/Yo/CV2/Ri/Ma/Tr cohort: abnormal in 93% (Psimaras 2010) — the Ri-specific cohort looked less inflammatory

normalPercentText: Brain MRI abnormal in 4/21; CT normal in 14/14 (Pittock 2003)
typicalFindings: Pontine T2 signal 2/21; one medial temporal/white matter/pontine enhancing pattern
Spinal MRI: cauda equina/lumbar root enhancement in 1/9

otherTests: Swallow/airway assessment if jaw dystonia or laryngospasm
pearls: 32% wheelchair-bound 1 month after onset, yet most improved after immunomodulatory or tumor-directed therapy (Pittock 2003)
Jaw dystonia can cause severe malnutrition; laryngospasm is an airway risk (Pittock 2010)

demographics: Median onset 61 y (26–85) (Peterson 1992, as cited by Jarius 2015)
Almost all female; in men, antigen expression by the tumor should be proven (PNS-Care)
cancerScreening: High-risk antibody: if initial screening is negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years (PNS-Care 2021)
Breast and pelvic (gynecologic) imaging; FDG-PET if conventional imaging is negative
PCD led to the cancer diagnosis in 63% (Rojas 2000)

rationale: Serum detection standard; PNS-Care recommends serum and CSF
methodNotes: Intracellular antigen: tissue IHC/IF with confirmatory immunoblot; confirm commercial line-blot positives with IHC, especially at low titer or with a mismatched phenotype (PNS-Care 2021)
Yo in a man or with an incongruent phenotype (e.g., seizures) — seek expert confirmatory testing (PNS-Care Table 4)

normalPercentText: Pooled Hu/Yo/CV2/Ri/Ma/Tr cohort: CSF abnormal in 93% (n=295); profile similar across antibody types (Psimaras 2010)
typicalFindings: Pleocytosis more often early: 47% before vs 28% after month 3; oligoclonal bands the only abnormality in 10%
Intrathecal anti-Yo synthesis (raised antibody index) in 5/5; CSF-restricted CDR2-specific oligoclonal bands in 9/9 (Jarius 2015)

normalPercentText: Normal at onset in 17/55 (31%) — Peterson 1992 cohort, as cited by Jarius 2015
typicalFindings: Acute MRI mostly normal; cerebellar atrophy at follow-up (Sanvito 2024 review table)

pearls: 94% became nonambulatory; no patient improved with cancer treatment or immunotherapy (Rojas 2000)
Median survival 100 months with breast vs 22 months with gynecologic cancer — tumor type drives survival
PCD progresses over weeks to months and stabilizes within ~6 months (Shams'ili 2003)

syndromes.syndrome: Limbic, diencephalic, or brainstem encephalitis (95% over follow-up); classic LE alone only 26%
Excessive daytime sleepiness (32%), sometimes narcolepsy-cataplexy with low CSF hypocretin
Eye movement abnormalities with brainstem involvement

demographics: Young men → testicular tumors and isolated Ma2; older patients → lung cancer, often with Ma1 + Ma2 (PNS-Care; Dalmau 2004)
cancerScreening: High-risk antibody: if initial screening is negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years (PNS-Care 2021)
Men: testicular ultrasound (microcalcification and cryptorchidism were risk markers in 2 patients without cancer); chest CT
Neurologic symptoms preceded tumor diagnosis in 62% (Dalmau 2004)

rationale: Antibodies present in serum and in all 13 CSF samples available (Dalmau 2004)
methodNotes: Intracellular antigen: tissue IHC/IF with confirmatory immunoblot; confirm commercial line-blot positives with IHC, especially at low titer or with a mismatched phenotype (PNS-Care 2021)
Additional Ma1 antibodies (15/38): more non-testicular tumors, ataxia, and worse prognosis

normalPercentText: Abnormal in 78% (25/32); normal cell count and protein in 7/32, 2 of whom had oligoclonal bands (Dalmau 2004)
typicalFindings: Pleocytosis 5–113 WBC/mm³ (median 20); protein 47–747 mg/dL (median 71)
CSF hypocretin can be low with hypersomnolence

normalPercentText: Abnormal in 74% overall; 89% with limbic or diencephalic dysfunction (Dalmau 2004)
typicalFindings: T2/FLAIR changes in medial temporal lobes, diencephalon/hypothalamus, or upper brainstem

otherTests: Sleep study / CSF hypocretin if hypersomnolent
pearls: Better outcome with male sex, age <45, testicular tumor with complete response, no Ma1 antibodies, limited CNS involvement
Immunosuppression wasn't associated with improvement overall but clearly helped some (Dalmau 2004)
MRI can mimic a tumor — test for Ma2 before biopsy

demographics: Median 61 y (14–75); 22/28 male (Bernal 2003)
cancerScreening: High-risk antibody: if initial screening is negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years (PNS-Care 2021)
CT chest/abdomen/pelvis ± FDG-PET for Hodgkin lymphoma

rationale: CSF positive with serum negative in 2/28 — send CSF (Bernal 2003)
methodNotes: DNER cell-based assay available (de Graaff 2012)
Antibodies disappeared spontaneously in all patients without tumor and in 10/10 after successful Hodgkin treatment — a negative later test doesn't exclude Tr-PCD

typicalFindings: Mild pleocytosis in 13/22 (median 50 cells, range 14–150)
Not reported systematically in Bernal 2003; cerebellar atrophy described in a late case

pearls: 22/28 had a subacute, irreversible severe cerebellar syndrome; 4 improved clearly
Age matters: complete remission in 3/7 aged ≤40 vs 1 partial remission among 21 older patients (Bernal 2003)
Tr immunoreactivity is usually absent in the tumor itself
sources: Graus F, et al. Updated diagnostic criteria for paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes (PNS-Care). Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2021;8:e1014. doi:10.1212/NXI.0000000000001014

syndromes.syndrome: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome with or without rapidly progressive cerebellar syndrome

cancerScreening: High-risk antibody: if initial screening is negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years (PNS-Care 2021)
Chest CT + FDG-PET for SCLC

rationale: LEMS: present in 64% with SCLC vs 0/50 idiopathic LEMS; also in 32% of Hu-positive SCLC and 22% of SCLC without a neurologic syndrome (Sabater 2008)
methodNotes: Utility of tissue IHC is unclear for SOX1 (PNS-Care)
Correlates with SCLC more than with any particular neurologic syndrome (PNS-Care)

pearls: SOX1 in a patient with LEMS strongly suggests SCLC — screen intensively even if the first search is negative
SOX1 is an independent SCLC predictor in LEMS alongside the DELTA-P items (Titulaer 2011)
sources: Graus F, et al. Updated diagnostic criteria for paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes (PNS-Care). Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2021;8:e1014. doi:10.1212/NXI.0000000000001014

syndromes.syndrome: Rhombencephalitis (brainstem/cerebellar): ataxia 82%, diplopia 56%, vertigo 54%, hearing loss 39%, tinnitus 36%, dysarthria 28%

demographics: All men; median 46 y (28–73) (Dubey 2020)

tumors.frequencyText: 80% (PNS-Care); of 36 screened: germ-cell tumor 64%, microlithiasis/fibrosis suggesting regressed tumor 19% (Dubey 2020)

cancerScreening: High-risk antibody: if initial screening is negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years (PNS-Care 2021)
Testicular ultrasound (look for microlithiasis/fibrosis as well as tumor); CT chest/abdomen/pelvis ± FDG-PET

rationale: PNS-Care recommends serum and CSF
methodNotes: Intracellular antigen: tissue IHC/IF with confirmatory immunoblot; confirm commercial line-blot positives with IHC, especially at low titer or with a mismatched phenotype (PNS-Care 2021)

typicalFindings: Median 10 cells/μL (0–86); median protein 65 mg/dL; supernumerary oligoclonal bands in 18/22 (82%)
T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in 76%: temporal 12, cerebellum 9, brainstem 3, diencephalon 3; enhancement in 3
Can look like a mass lesion → misdiagnosed as tumor/metastasis
Follow-up >2 y: cerebellar atrophy 6/12; hypertrophic olivary degeneration 3

pearls: Hearing loss or tinnitus preceded other deficits by 1–8 months in 26% — think of it in a young man with new sensorineural loss plus ataxia
Often refractory; wheelchair dependence more likely when no testicular cancer is found; outcomes similar to Ma2 (Dubey 2020)
sources: Graus F, et al. Updated diagnostic criteria for paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes (PNS-Care). Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2021;8:e1014. doi:10.1212/NXI.0000000000001014

Dubey D, et al. Expanded clinical phenotype, oncological associations, and immunopathologic insights of paraneoplastic Kelch-like protein-11 encephalitis. JAMA Neurol 2020;77(11):1420-1429. doi:10.1001/jamaneurol.2020.2231

cancerScreening: High-risk antibody: if initial screening is negative, repeat every 4–6 months for 2 years (PNS-Care 2021)
Chest CT ± FDG-PET for SCLC

rationale: Cohort defined mainly by serum (92 of 96 archived specimens) (Gadoth 2017)
methodNotes: Intracellular antigen: tissue IHC with confirmatory testing (PNS-Care)
Often accompanied by other SCLC markers: CRMP5 26%, VGCC 22%, Hu 13% (Gadoth 2017)

typicalFindings: Pleocytosis in 15/29 (52%, median 20 cells); raised protein in 21/29 (74%, median 60 mg/dL) (Gadoth 2017)

normalPercentText: Brain/spine MRI normal in 15/43 (35%); nonspecific white-matter change in 8 more (Gadoth 2017)
typicalFindings: Pathologic in 46%: spinal cord T2 lesions/enhancement, cerebral atrophy, optic nerve or temporal lobe involvement, meningeal enhancement

pearls: Physician-reported benefit from immunotherapy in 14/26; some neurologic benefit after chemotherapy in 11/15 (Gadoth 2017)
Detection rate similar to amphiphysin and higher than Ri or Tr — worth including in paraneoplastic panels
sources: Graus F, et al. Updated diagnostic criteria for paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes (PNS-Care). Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2021;8:e1014. doi:10.1212/NXI.0000000000001014

syndromes.syndrome: Optic neuritis (often severe, posterior, bilateral; chiasm/tract)
Acute myelitis — single longitudinally extensive lesion across the cord's transverse diameter
Area postrema syndrome (intractable hiccups, nausea, vomiting)
Acute brainstem, diencephalic (symptomatic narcolepsy), or cerebral syndromes

demographics: Female > male; pediatric onset extremely rare (Banwell 2023 Table 1)
Paraneoplastic AQP4: older age, male, severe nausea/vomiting at onset (PNS-Care)
cancerScreening: Comprehensive cancer screening at initial diagnosis is sufficient for lower-risk antibodies (PNS-Care 2021)

rationale: Diagnosis rests on positive serum AQP4-IgG by cell-based assay plus ≥1 core clinical characteristic (Wingerchuk 2015)
methodNotes: Cell-based assay recommended (Wingerchuk 2015)

typicalFindings: CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands infrequent (5–20%) vs >80% in MS (Banwell 2023 Table 1)
Pleocytosis can be marked
Brain MRI might be normal with optic neuritis or myelitis presentations (Banwell 2023 Table 1)
Lesions in AQP4-rich regions: peri-third/fourth ventricle, splenium, internal capsule, dorsal medulla; patchy cloud-like or pencil-thin ependymal enhancement
Spinal cord: bright spotty lesions; residual T1-hypointense lesions might be present (21–50%)
Banwell 2023 Table 1 frequency bands: infrequent 5–20%, might be present 21–50%

otherTests: MRI orbits and whole spine with contrast
pearls: Risk of poor visual recovery and of worsening motor impairment with relapses (Banwell 2023 Table 1) — treat attacks urgently
Interferon-beta, natalizumab, and fingolimod can worsen NMOSD
sources: Wingerchuk DM, et al. International consensus diagnostic criteria for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders. Neurology 2015;85(2):177-189. doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000001729

syndromes.syndrome: Optic neuritis — frequently bilateral, anterior, longitudinally extensive, with optic nerve sheath enhancement and disc edema
Myelitis — longitudinally extensive or multiple; gray-matter H-sign; conus lesions
Cerebral cortical encephalitis with seizures; brainstem/cerebellar syndromes

demographics: Female = male; pediatric onset frequent (Banwell 2023 Table 1)
cancerScreening: Comprehensive cancer screening at initial diagnosis is sufficient for lower-risk antibodies (PNS-Care 2021)

rationale: Serum is the preferred specimen; CSF positivity in seropositive MOGAD ranged 42–61% in cited series (Banwell 2023)
CSF-only positives occur rarely and can support MOGAD in seronegative patients with supportive clinical/MRI features
methodNotes: Live cell-based assay preferred; fixed CBA acceptable; ELISA not recommended (Banwell 2023)
Fixed CBA: clear positive ≥1:100; low positive 1:10 to <1:100 — low positives need AQP4-IgG negativity plus ≥1 supporting clinical or MRI feature
Test before steroids/IVIG/PLEX when possible; if negative but suspicion high, repeat ≥3 months later or at relapse
Titers usually fall over time but can stay positive for years

typicalFindings: CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands infrequent (5–20%) vs >80% in MS (Banwell 2023 Table 1)
Brain MRI might be normal with optic neuritis or myelitis presentations
Fluffy, poorly demarcated T2 lesions in white matter, deep gray matter, middle cerebellar peduncle; partial or complete resolution expected; T1-hypointense residua extremely rare (<5%)
Leptomeningeal enhancement around brainstem; unilateral/bilateral cortical leptomeningeal enhancement with cortical encephalitis
Banwell 2023 Table 1 frequency bands: infrequent 5–20%, might be present 21–50%

otherTests: AQP4-IgG (negative result needed to interpret low-positive MOG)
pearls: Course monophasic or relapsing; recovery after attacks typically favorable (vision, motor), though residual sphincter/erectile dysfunction can follow myelitis (Banwell 2023 Table 1)
False positives more likely with low titers — don't diagnose MOGAD from a low positive in an MS-like picture

syndromes.syndrome: Meningoencephalomyelitis — meningitis, encephalitis, myelitis, or combinations (81%)

demographics: Median onset 44 y (8–103); 54% women (Flanagan 2017)
cancerScreening: Comprehensive cancer screening at initial diagnosis is sufficient for lower-risk antibodies (PNS-Care 2021)
Pelvic imaging for ovarian teratoma — predicted best when NMDAR-IgG and AQP4-IgG coexist (71%) (Flanagan 2017)

rationale: Paired samples: CSF positive 45/49 (92%) vs serum 22/49 (45%); CSF testing had the highest specificity for meningoencephalomyelitis (94%) (Flanagan 2017)
methodNotes: GFAPα-IgG is the most sensitive isoform (100%)
Rare false positives in controls: serum tissue assay 0.5%, serum CBA 1.5%, CSF CBA 0.9% — serum-only positives are less specific

typicalFindings: Median 78.5 cells (13–550), lymphocyte-predominant; protein raised in 30/36 (median 80 mg/dL); low glucose in 4/22; CSF-restricted OCB in 13/24
Linear perivascular radial enhancement extending from the ventricles in 53%; also leptomeningeal (22%), serpentine (19%), ependymal (9%)
Spinal cord: longitudinally extensive lesions common; central canal enhancement in 21%
DWI normal in all evaluated; lesions often resolve with steroids

otherTests: NMDAR-IgG and AQP4-IgG (coexist; affect tumor risk)
Vessel imaging if vasculitis is suspected — angiography was normal in all tested
pearls: Improved with corticosteroids in 14/16 — but relapses during taper (often below prednisone 20 mg/day) or after stopping steroid-sparing therapy; plan steroid-sparing maintenance (Flanagan 2017)
Mimics CNS vasculitis on imaging (32% considered) — angiography was uniformly negative
